verses.pali: “Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo tassapāhaṁ lābhasakkārasiloko antarāyāya vadāmī”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants, possessions, honor, and popularity are an obstacle even for a mendicant who is perfected, with defilements ended.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

verses.pali: “kissa pana, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno lābhasakkārasiloko antarāyāyā”ti?
verses.english: “Sir, what do possessions, honor, and popularity obstruct for a mendicant with defilements ended?”

verses.pali: “Yā hissa sā, ānanda, akuppā cetovimutti nāhaṁ tassā lābhasakkārasilokaṁ antarāyāya vadāmi.
verses.english: “Ānanda, I don’t say that possessions, honor, and popularity obstruct the unshakable freedom of heart.

verses.pali: Ye ca khvassa, ānanda, appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārā adhigatā tesāhamassa lābhasakkārasilokaṁ antarāyāya vadāmi.
verses.english: But I do say that possessions, honor, and popularity obstruct the achievement of blissful meditations in this life for a meditator who is diligent, keen, and resolute.

verses.pali: Evaṁ dāruṇo kho, ānanda, lābhasakkārasiloko kaṭuko pharuso antarāyiko anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya.
verses.english: So grim are possessions, honor, and popularity—bitter and harsh, an obstacle to reaching the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.
So you should train like this:

verses.pali: ‘uppannaṁ lābhasakkārasilokaṁ pajahissāma, na ca no uppanno lābhasakkārasiloko cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘We will give up arisen possessions, honor, and popularity, and we won’t let them occupy our minds.’
